To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amphiphilicity of hexakisadduct derivatives of C60 can be controlled by the choice of the polar addend and the charge of the polar terminus.

we have synthesized a variety of new hexakisadduct C60 derivatives with mixed octahedral addition patterns and have shown by TEM and NMR that the amphiphilicity of the [3:3]:hexakisadduct C 60 derivatives can be controlled by pH.

we have prepared and characterized a variety (i.e. different polar groups) of amphiphilic C60 hexakisadduct, which are soluble in water in charged forms, and that the aggregation properties of these compounds are pH-dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of amphiphilic fullerene derivatives.
the preparation of amphiphilic C-60 derivatives with the aim of developing novel supramolecular systems based on the self-assembly of C-60.
the preparation of amphiphilic fullerenes with the aim of developing new functionalized materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synthesis of a large variety of amphiphilic fullerenes is possible.
the [5:1]:[3:3]-ratio is a very important one, because it is a key parameter for the solubility and for the self-assembling properties of the adducts.
the [3:3:6]-trisadducts of the type 1-4 and 7-12 are not suitable for use as building blocks for amphiphilic C60 adducts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have synthesized and characterized new hexakisadduct of C60 involving the mixed octahedral 5:1 and 3:3-addition patterns.
we have prepared and studied a series of new amphiphiles based on C60 and that we were able to control the aggregation behavior of these molecules by variation of the charge of the polar termini.
amphiphilic C-60 derivatives can be prepared in a very flexible way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amphiphilicity of the [3:3]:[5:1]-hexakisaddends is strongly influenced by the nature of the polar group.
amphiphilic C60 derivatives are very promising building blocks for nanomaterials, which can be tuned to a large extent by the choice of polar and non-polar addend.
the amphiphilics [5:1], [3:3], and [2:2:2]-hexakisaddends are very soluble in aqueous solutions.
